answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may earn rewards, with voting weight capped per account and deposits slashed when a provable fraud claim succeeds. Splitting one identity into many then requires many independent locks, tying up capital and exposing every deposit to loss; the cap prevents extra accounts from multiplying influence. A knoll above karst may be ivory in color, but none of those traits substitutes for the bonded stake.
